A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Utonia: Toward One Encoder for All Point Clouds. All 15 pages, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A.1–A.3, support reliable comparison; no material gaps were found.

before.justification: v1 reports original Utonia experiments and ablations, including point-cloud perception, simulated robotic manipulation and spatial reasoning results in Tables 2–10.

after.justification: v2 reports the same original Utonia experiments and ablations in Tables 2–10, with implementation details in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The modality blinding, perceptual granularity rescaling, RoPE-enhanced encoder and downstream integration procedures are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: The pretraining mixture in Table 12 and evaluation coverage are unchanged, including indoor/outdoor segmentation, object classification and part segmentation, manipulation, and spatial reasoning.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the reported experiments. Removing the words 'the baseline' before Video-3D LLM in Section 4.2 does not change its role or the comparisons in Table 10.

E3.justification: Data splits, model sizes, probing and fine-tuning protocols, metrics, and downstream testing procedures remain unchanged. The new Appendix A.3 cross-reference points to settings already present in v1.

E4.justification: The grid-size study in Table 2, missing-modality tests in Table 6, ablations in Table 7, and qualitative analyses in Figures 1–3 and 5–6 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting without introducing seed counts, across-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 9 retains manipulation success rates of 74.7, 80.0 and 82.1 for Sonata, Concerto and Utonia; v2 merely adds an explicit reference to this existing table.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 preserves Equations 1–5 defining coordinate jitter, scaling and separable 3D RoPE. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about a shared encoder, cross-domain benefits, emergent behaviors and downstream applications. Contribution scope and novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and interpretations of the experimental findings are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same discussion of task-specific readouts, dynamic-scene extensions and backbone efficiency constraints.

D1.justification: Appendices A.1–A.3 retain identical data preparation, training, hardware, architecture and downstream implementation details. The project link is unchanged; the added appendix pointer discloses no new technical information.

R1.justification: Section 5 and all 62 references are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to previous point-cloud pretraining and positional-encoding methods.

P1.justification: Section 4.2 adds references to Table 9 and Appendix A.3, changes 'robotics tasks' to 'robotic tasks', and removes 'the baseline' before Video-3D LLM. The acknowledgment adds Jinfeng Xie, and the version/date stamp changes. There is no document reorganization.

P2.justification: Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–12 retain identical displays, captions and placement. Page structure is unchanged; the small prose edits only alter local line wrapping.

improvement.justification: The added cross-references marginally ease navigation to Table 9 and Appendix A.3, both already present in v1. With scientific content, results, implementation details and organization unchanged, the small wording and acknowledgment edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
